meta.name: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Associate (1Z0-1085-24)
meta.notes: Initial release — OCI Foundations 2024 (1Z0-1085-24): regions/ADs/FDs, IAM compartments and policies, VCN networking, compute shapes, block and object storage, Autonomous Database, Vault, Free Tier, and pricing models.

questions.question: An architect is designing a highly available deployment on OCI and must place resources correctly across the provider's physical hierarchy. How does OCI's physical hierarchy of regions, availability domains (ADs), and fault domains (FDs) work?
options: A region contains one or more ADs; each AD is divided into three fault domains
A region always contains exactly three ADs; each AD contains a single fault domain
A region contains a single AD; fault domains span across ADs for redundancy
A region equals an AD; fault domains are logical groupings of multiple regions
questions.explanation: An OCI region contains one or more availability domains (each AD is an isolated data centre). Inside every AD there are three fault domains, which are independent groupings of hardware that act as failure isolation zones within the AD. Some newer regions are single-AD, while many commercial regions have three ADs.

questions.question: A finance team needs strict isolation of their OCI resources from engineering, but both groups must roll up to the tenancy's overall cost dashboard. Which OCI construct best fits?
options: Separate OCI tenancies for finance and engineering
Separate compartments under the same tenancy
Separate VCNs with no peering between them
Separate availability domains for each team
questions.explanation: Compartments are logical containers used to organise, isolate, and control access to resources within a single tenancy; policies on compartments enforce isolation while billing still aggregates at the tenancy level. Separate tenancies would split billing entirely, VCNs only isolate networking (not other resources), and ADs are physical infrastructure rather than an organisational boundary.

questions.question: Which statement is valid OCI IAM policy syntax to let members of the group NetAdmins manage Virtual Cloud Networks in the compartment Network?
options: allow user NetAdmins to manage virtual-network-family in compartment Network
allow group NetAdmins to manage virtual-network-family in compartment Network
permit group NetAdmins manage vcn in compartment Network
grant group NetAdmins all on virtual-network-family in compartment Network
questions.explanation: OCI policy syntax is: Allow <subject> to <verb> <resource-type> in <location> [where <conditions>]. The subject is normally a group or dynamic group, the verb is inspect/read/use/manage, and virtual-network-family is the aggregate resource type covering VCNs, subnets, gateways, and route tables. Allowing 'user' directly is rare, and 'permit'/'grant' are not valid OCI keywords.

questions.question: You are designing a VCN whose workload must span multiple availability domains for high availability. What is the simplest subnet design?
options: Create one AD-specific subnet per AD and manually replicate resources
Create regional subnets, which span all availability domains in the region
Create one subnet per fault domain across the region
Use a single AD-specific subnet and rely on cross-region replication
questions.explanation: Regional subnets stretch across every AD in a region, so the same CIDR can host resources in any AD and multi-AD HA designs need only one subnet per tier. AD-specific subnets are a legacy option that force multiple subnets and more IP planning, fault domains do not have their own subnets, and cross-region replication addresses disaster recovery rather than in-region HA.

questions.question: An OCI compute instance in a private subnet must pull packages from Oracle YUM repositories on the Oracle Services Network without sending the traffic over the public internet. Which gateway provides this?
options: Internet Gateway
NAT Gateway
Service Gateway
Dynamic Routing Gateway (DRG)
questions.explanation: A Service Gateway lets VCN resources reach supported Oracle Services Network endpoints (such as Object Storage and Oracle YUM mirrors) over the Oracle backbone, never traversing the public internet. An Internet Gateway provides bidirectional public-internet access, a NAT Gateway provides egress-only public-internet access, and a DRG connects a VCN to on-premises networks or other VCNs.

questions.question: While sizing compute instances in OCI, an architect is deciding between flexible and fixed shapes and reviews how they differ. Which statement BEST describes the difference between flexible and fixed compute shapes in OCI?
options: Flexible shapes let you independently choose OCPU count and memory; fixed shapes use predetermined values
Flexible shapes can be resized while the instance is running; fixed shapes always require a stop and start
Flexible shapes are only available on Ampere ARM processors; fixed shapes are only AMD and Intel
Flexible shapes are billed monthly; fixed shapes are billed per second
questions.explanation: Flexible shapes such as VM.Standard.E4.Flex and VM.Standard.A1.Flex let you pick the exact number of OCPUs and the amount of memory when you provision the instance. Fixed shapes such as VM.Standard2.4 come with a preset CPU and memory configuration. Resizing both types still typically requires a stop, both shape families exist on AMD, Intel, and Ampere, and OCI uses the same per-second billing model for either.

questions.question: For a workload that needs the highest IOPS per gigabyte on OCI Block Volumes, which elastic performance tier should you select?
options: Lower Cost
Balanced
Higher Performance
Ultra High Performance
questions.explanation: OCI Block Volume offers four elastic performance tiers. Ultra High Performance (UHP) targets the most demanding workloads and delivers the highest IOPS-per-GB ratio. Higher Performance offers about 75 IOPS/GB, Balanced (the default) about 60 IOPS/GB, and Lower Cost about 10 IOPS/GB and is suited to cold or archival data.

questions.question: Which OCI Object Storage tier is designed for data that is rarely accessed and can tolerate restore delays measured in hours, at the lowest storage cost?
options: Standard tier
Infrequent Access tier
Archive tier
Auto-Tiering
questions.explanation: The Archive tier delivers the lowest storage cost and is intended for data that is rarely accessed; objects must be restored before download and restoration typically takes hours. Standard is for active data, Infrequent Access lowers cost for occasionally accessed data with no restore delay, and Auto-Tiering automatically moves Standard objects between hot and infrequent access patterns rather than being a cold-storage tier of its own.

questions.question: A team is choosing between Oracle Autonomous Database and a self-managed OCI Database System and wants to know what they gain that the self-managed option cannot match. Which capability is unique to Oracle Autonomous Database compared with a self-managed OCI Database System?
options: Automated patching, backups, scaling, and tuning fully managed by Oracle
Support for the SQL language and PL/SQL
Multi-AD high availability via Data Guard
Pay-per-use OCPU-hour billing
questions.explanation: Autonomous Database is a self-driving managed database whose distinguishing feature is automation of patching, backups, scaling, and performance tuning by Oracle. SQL and PL/SQL are supported by both Autonomous and self-managed Database Systems, multi-AD Data Guard configurations are available on both, and pay-per-use billing applies to both as well.

questions.question: A student wants to run a small Autonomous Database and a Compute instance indefinitely on OCI without being billed. Which description of Always Free resources is correct?
options: They are only usable during the 30-day Free Trial period and disabled afterwards
They are available indefinitely at no cost within published limits, even after the trial ends
They require a paid subscription but include 300 US dollars in monthly credits
They are only available in OCI Government Cloud regions
questions.explanation: OCI's Always Free programme provides resources such as two AMD VM.Standard.E2.1.Micro instances, two Autonomous Databases, 200 GB of Block Volume, and 20 GB of Object Storage that remain free indefinitely within published quotas, even after the 30-day Free Trial expires. The separate Free Trial provides a one-time US$300 credit usable against paid services and lasts 30 days; both make up the OCI Free Tier.

questions.question: Which OCI service should be used to centrally generate, store, and rotate encryption keys and secrets such as database passwords?
options: OCI Vault
OCI Bastion
OCI Identity Domains
OCI Audit
questions.explanation: OCI Vault is a managed service that creates and manages master encryption keys (optionally HSM-backed) and stores secrets like passwords or API tokens with versioning and rotation. OCI Bastion brokers secure SSH or RDP sessions into private resources, Identity Domains is the IAM identity layer for users and federation, and Audit captures API activity logs for compliance.

questions.question: A customer commits to a one-year spend with Oracle in exchange for discounted rates and the freedom to consume any OCI service against that committed amount. Which pricing model is this?
options: Pay As You Go (PAYG)
Annual Universal Credits
Bring Your Own License (BYOL)
Government Cloud pricing
questions.explanation: Annual Universal Credits represent a committed annual spend that can be applied to any OCI service at discounted rates compared with PAYG. PAYG is on-demand consumption with no commitment, BYOL lets customers re-use existing on-premises Oracle licences to lower OCI database or middleware costs, and Government Cloud pricing applies to a separate region offering for US government workloads.
